grades.reason: Describes RISC-V vector segment load/store instructions; it says nothing about page-stride access or why such access would be slow.

grades.quote: the MMU has a TLB in which it keeps track of recently used virtual-to-physical translations; repeated access to the same virtual page number doesn’t require access to the page table. Only when a new page number is accessed is the page table (of whatever kind) accessed.
grades.reason: Explains the TLB mechanism. An access to the same page needs no page table lookup, but an access to a new page does. This implies that a one-page stride touches a new page each time, causing TLB misses and page table walks. It doesn't directly mention strided array access.
Covers how linear page tables are stored and how the recursion problem is avoided. It doesn't address performance with page-stride access or the TLB.

grades.quote: Otherwise, the performance will be intolerably slow, because of disk accesses made on a routine basis.
grades.reason: Gives a secondary possible cause: if the touched pages exceed the RAM working set, paging to disk makes access very slow. It doesn't tie this to a one-page stride.
